summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Shoko Takeuchi studied at Ryukoku University. He later served as an emeritus professor at Ryukoku University, attested between 1987 and 1995, and was also attested there in 2009.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Shoko Watanabe studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernst Leumann and Naoshiro Tsuji, and earned a doctorate at Toyo University. He held professorships at Taisho University (1935–1943) and Toyo University (1956–1969).

A researcher in Buddhist studies and Indology, Shoku Bando studied at Kyoto University of Education, Otani University, and the University of Freiburg (1984–1986). In 1987, he held appointments at the Abhidharma Institute, Kyoto University, and Fukui Prefectural College.

Working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Shoren Ihara served as an assistant professor at Kyushu University (attested 1959–1965, and attested again in 1977). He was later a member of the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1996–1998).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, Shoryu Katsura earned degrees from Kyoto University and the University of Toronto. He served as professor at Hiroshima University (1976–2004) and Ryukoku University (2004–2015), alongside visiting appointments at Berkeley and Calgary.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Shoshin Fukihara studied at Otani University under Susumu Yamaguchi and at Hōryūji Kangakuin under Join Saeki. He held teaching posts at Otani University, Otani Senshu Gakuin, Shinshu College, Doho University, and Otani University Junior College.

Working in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, Shoshin Higuchi served as a lecturer at Otani University (attested 1998) and as a committee member for the Otani Academic Society (attested 2000).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Shoshin Ichishima served at Taisho University, where he was Dean of Academic Affairs (attested 1983) and later Professor Emeritus (attested 2014). He was also a visiting lecturer in Tibetan Buddhism at the University of Hawaiʻi.

Specializing in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies, Shoshin Kuwayama studied at Kyoto University from around 1957 to 1966. He subsequently served as an assistant professor at Kyoto University from circa 1966 to 2002.

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, Shoson Miyamoto studied at Otani University, the University of Tokyo, and the University of Oxford. He was a professor at the University of Tokyo, Komazawa University, Toyo University, and Waseda University.

A specialist in history, archaeology, and Sinology, Shou-chien Shih served as a professor at National Taiwan University from approximately 1990 to 2003. He was also the director of the National Palace Museum from around 2004 to 2006.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Shoyu Hanayama studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1950 to 1954. He later served as vice president of Musashino University (~1968–1995) and chairperson of the Society for the Promotion of Buddhism (~1987–1995).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Shozen Kumoi studied at Otani University and under Erich Frauwallner. He was an assistant and emeritus professor at Otani University (1948–1981, ~1986–2017) and a professor at Bukkyo University in 1982.
Specializing in philosophy and Indology, Shri Krishna Saksena held appointments as a professor at the University of Lucknow and at the University of Hawaiʻi, both attested in 2016.
A scholar in Indology and linguistics, Shri Krishna Sharma founded the Hindu Maha Sabha and DAV College, Suva. He also taught the scholar Dieter Schuh.

A scholar of Indology, Shridhar Ramakrishna Bhandarkar served as Assistant to the Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College in 1884. He subsequently held posts as Professor of Sanskrit at Elphinstone College and permanent Professor of Sanskrit at Wilson College, Mumbai.

A scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies, Shrikant S. Bahulkar studied under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale. He served as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and held a post at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (attested 2000).

A scholar of Indology and philosophy, Shripad Krishna Belvalkar studied under Kashinath Bapu Pathak. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (~1904–1927), honorary secretary at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1918–1927), and General Secretary of the All-India Oriental Conference.

Specializing in Indology and religious studies, Shrivatsa Goswami studied philosophy at Banaras Hindu University, where he also taught philosophy and religion. He was a visiting scholar at Harvard University and held a post at the Vrindaban Research Institute (attested 1994).

A scholar in linguistics and Indology, Shu-Fen Chen studied at National Tsing Hua University under Chin-Fa Lien, completing doctoral research under Hans Henrich Hock. She served as a professor at National Tsing Hua University (attested 2010).
